pillar_reactions.evidence: Accepted without resistance — 'Makes sense, yes' and, asked for his thoughts, 'Nothing. Ready to learn.' He had already validated it himself: one month of kettlebell work off free videos 'has helped me a lot with my back pain'. When asked later which element would help most, he chose this one: 'definitely the mobility, everything is going to make me feel better.'

Engaged hardest here and asked repeatedly for detail, particularly on fasting — 'I thought you were going to say, like, in a video, I saw him say something about fasting 38 hours', then 'so fasting is recommended to do that every day, or is that like once a week, once a month?' He needed the distinction between intermittent fasting and extended fasting spelled out before he was comfortable.

Accepted with a one-word confirmation ('Check') and no questions. The video-feedback element was the part he had come for: 'definitely sending the videos, because that's like my biggest interest, just know if I'm doing a correct technique.'

anchors.raw: since I've been practicing also, I feel, so I had this herniated disc since many years ago. And I can say like, this has helped me a lot with my back pain.
anchors.note: The fifth prospect in this batch already getting results from the provider's free content before any price conversation — and here the free version has partially solved a years-old chronic pain problem in a month. The rep amplified it rather than repositioning it: 'imagine if you keep doing it for like another five, right?'

anchors.raw: I was expecting like maximum, I don't know, maybe a hundred a month
anchors.note: A stated ceiling of roughly $100 a month against a $6,000 six-month price. The gap is a factor of ten and no payment structure closes it.

anchors.note: Recently cleared arrears more than double the price of the programme, and is currently taking a loan to pay a university semester. Capacity is genuinely absent rather than being withheld.

anchors.note: His reference class for coaching is gym-floor personal trainers in Ecuador, a substantially cheaper market. His objection to them was philosophical — they pushed toward enhanced bodybuilding and he wants to stay natural — which is a differentiation opening the rep used well.

anchors.raw: I actually bought recently a kettlebell and I've been practicing at my gym
anchors.note: He already pays for a gym and owns a kettlebell, so equipment and venue are sunk costs and the programme has to justify itself purely as instruction.

unmet_demand.want: Form correction and technique coaching for kettlebell work at around $100 a month
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Nothing exists at that price, and the rep said so explicitly rather than downselling: 'the lowest thing that we have is university, but that's also not where you're going to actually get the form that you would need, and for you, it's very important that you do go onto the one-to-one.' The company has no product for a highly motivated prospect with no money.

unmet_demand.want: Training that is safe and appropriate for a diagnosed herniated disc under active medical treatment
unmet_demand.why_unmet: There is no clinical screening, no referral pathway and no coordination with the doctor already treating him. The condition was answered with training claims — 'that's also how the pain actually stays away' — rather than with a clearance step.

unmet_demand.want: A clear answer on whether kettlebell programming rotates workouts the way gym splits do
unmet_demand.why_unmet: He asked directly and got 'It depends. Like, overall, we have definitely switching routines. It depends a little bit on which person you're specifically working with.' The question was never actually answered before the conversation moved to price.

unmet_demand.want: Guidance on abdominal 'inflammation' he attributes to a previous powerlifting bulk
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Raised twice and never explored. The rep offered a one-line speculation — 'you probably overeat as well' — and moved on. Whether this is a nutrition issue, a training issue or a clinical one was never established.
